stories.title: Lincoln, PGIM Acquire Two DFW Medical Buildings
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company and PGIM acquired two outpatient medical buildings in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, totaling 103,000 square feet. Acquired through separate transactions, the portfolio includes 17051 N. Dallas Parkway in Addison, Texas (shown) and the Rayzor Ranch Medical Building in Denton, Texas. SRP Medical was the seller of the Addison building, and Prime Denton Properties was the seller of the Denton facility. The Class A outpatient medical buildings are immediately adjacent to acute care and surgical hospital campuses. Collectively, the properties are 84% leased to a diverse tenant roster that includes Texas Health Resources, Methodist Health System, and leading physician groups specializing in outpatient surgery, primary care, orthopedics, neurosurgery, pain management, gastroenterology, dermatology, ophthalmology, mammography, and behavioral health. Positioned within established healthcare nodes along two of the Metroplex’s fastest-growing corridors, the acquisitions provide Lincoln’s national healthcare investment platform with additional scale in North Texas. PGIM’s Real Estate Investment Group has $217 billion in gross assets under management and administration. The post Lincoln, PGIM Acquire Two DFW Medical Buildings appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property and PGIM acquired 103k SF medical buildings in Addison and Denton, Texas.
Properties 84% leased to healthcare tenants near acute care campuses in high-growth corridors.
Consolidates institutional capital focus on North Texas healthcare nodes alongside hospital networks.
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company and PGIM acquired two Class A outpatient medical buildings totaling 103,000 square feet in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex—one in Addison and one in Denton—positioned adjacent to acute care campuses. Both properties are 84% leased to diverse healthcare operators including Texas Health Resources, Methodist Health System, and physician groups. The acquisitions anchor institutional healthcare investment in two of North Texas's fastest-growing corridors.
stories.impact: Signals robust institutional capital flow into North Texas healthcare real estate tied to hospital expansions and population inflow. This capital consolidation around medical nodes may lift land values and development feasibility for multifamily in adjacent mixed-use areas where medical workers, patients, and service workers will drive residential demand in DFW submarkets like Addison and Denton.

stories.title: Starwood Capital Group Hires Blackstone’s Michael Eglit as U.S. Head of Originations
stories.excerpt: Fall is almost here and a slight chill — plus the scent of freshly sharpened pencils — is in the air. For Starwood Capital Group, there’s also a new leader at the helm of its debt business as the firm gears up for the fourth quarter. Starwood Capital has hired Michael Eglit as its new head of U.S. originations, sources confirmed to Commercial Observer. Previously, Eglit spent almost 15 years at Blackstone, most recently as head of U.S. originations for Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. Commercial Mortgage Alert reported last month that the move was in the works. Eglit’s first day was Sept. 8 — he’ll be splitting his time between Greenwich, Conn., and New York City — and his move comes roughly 17 months after Jonathan Pollack, Eglit’s former Blackstone colleague, joined Starwood Capital Group as president. With that familiarity as the foundation, sources familiar with the move said that Eglit becoming part of the Starwood team was a very natural fit from a cultural point of view. As one source put it, “Starwood’s got one of the most pre-eminent debt businesses in the country, and Mike’s goal is to now come in and help make it even bigger and better.” Eglit brings plenty of new relationships to Starwood’s table, the source said, adding that the majority of Starwood’s loans are to repeat borrowers and the firm has lost its fair share to Blackstone as a competitor over the years. Now Eglit can bring some of those relationships Starwood couldn’t penetrate into the fold. “People do business with people that they know, they like and they trust, and Starwood just added that additional element in those relationships that didn’t exist before, which will be impactful to their business,” the source said, adding that the team is already looking at deals that they’ve never looked at or won previously with Eglit onboard. bullets: Starwood Capital hired Blackstone's Michael Eglit as U.S. head of originations for debt business.
Eglit spent 15 years at Blackstone leading real estate debt originations before move Sept. 8.
Follows Jonathan Pollack's 2023 move from Blackstone to Starwood as president.
stories.summary: Starwood Capital Group hired Michael Eglit, formerly head of U.S. originations for Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies, as its new head of U.S. originations, effective September 8. Eglit brings 15 years of Blackstone experience and follows Jonathan Pollack's move to Starwood as president roughly 17 months prior. The leadership shift reflects Starwood's strategic buildup of its debt origination platform ahead of Q4 activity.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. The move signals competitive talent poaching between major debt platforms but does not materially change lending availability, rates, or debt terms for developers. Monitor Starwood's debt strategy in coming quarters for any shift in multifamily lending appetite or pricing.

stories.title: Magnet Maker Building $1.2B Plant West of Charlotte
stories.excerpt: USA Rare Earth broke ground on a $1.2 billion magnet manufacturing facility in Blacksburg, South Carolina, 45 minutes west of Charlotte. The facility will create 490 jobs. The magnets and refined metals produced in Blacksburg will support needs in the defense, aerospace, semiconductor, medical, AI, energy and advanced manufacturing industries. Blacksburg was selected for its power access, workforce and construction timeline. Duke Energy says it can accommodate the power needs. The company plans to have the 800,000-square-foot facility’s shell built by 2027, with operations online in April 2028. Trammell Crow is the project’s developer, with Clark Construction and Frampton Construction serving as general contractors. McMillan Pazdan Smith is the architect. USA Rare Earth will lease its facility for a 20-year term. The company has two options to extend the lease — each for an additional 10 years. This will be the company’s second manufacturing facility. It has an existing plant in Stillwater, Oklahoma. The post Magnet Maker Building $1.2B Plant West of Charlotte appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: USA Rare Earth breaking ground on $1.2B magnet plant in Blacksburg, SC, 45 min west of Charlotte.
800k SF facility creating 490 jobs; operational April 2028; Trammell Crow is developer.
Defense, aerospace, semiconductor, AI, energy demand; 20-year lease with two 10-year extension options.
stories.summary: USA Rare Earth broke ground on a $1.2 billion, 800,000-square-foot magnet and refined metals manufacturing facility in Blacksburg, South Carolina, 45 minutes west of Charlotte. The facility will create 490 jobs and reach operations in April 2028. Trammell Crow is the developer; the company will lease the facility for 20 years with two optional 10-year extensions. Production supports defense, aerospace, semiconductor, AI, energy, and advanced manufacturing sectors.
stories.impact: Major positive signal for multifamily demand in the Charlotte metro submarket and surrounding Catawba County/Blacksburg area. 490 high-wage manufacturing jobs in advanced tech will draw in-migration; workers will demand housing within 20–30 minutes of the plant. Recommend evaluating residential sites in North Charlotte suburbs, Fort Mill (SC), and along I-85 corridor for workforce housing and market-rate luxury product. Expect sustained demand growth through 2028 and beyond as facility ramps operations.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges $55M Refinancing for Seattle Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Newmark has arranged a $55 million loan on behalf of Mack Real Estate Group, Silverstein Properties and Cantor Fitzgerald to refinance Swell Apartments, a 200-unit multifamily community in Seattle, Washington. Newmark’s Co-Head of Global Debt & Structured Finance, Jordan Roeschlaub; Vice Chairman, Chris Kramer; Senior Associate, Sam Speciale; and Analyst, Lance Tillman arranged the financing with ORIX. Completed in 2024, Swell Apartments is a newly constructed luxury apartment community located in Seattle’s Yesler Terrace neighborhood. The 200-unit property offers a mix of market-rate and affordable residences with contemporary finishes, including stainless steel appliances, floor-to-ceiling windows and in-unit laundry. Positioned within one of Seattle’s most connected residential neighborhoods, the property offers immediate access to the Seattle Streetcar and Interstate 5, providing convenient connectivity to downtown Seattle and the region’s leading employment centers. Swell Apartments is also located near major employers, including Amazon, Microsoft, Costco and Starbucks, as well as the city’s entertainment and cultural destinations. bullets: Newmark arranged $55M ORIX refinancing for Swell Apartments, 200-unit luxury in Seattle Yesler Terrace.
Newly completed 2024; mix of market-rate and affordable units near Amazon, Microsoft, Costco.

stories.summary: Newmark arranged a $55 million refinancing loan from ORIX on behalf of Mack Real Estate Group, Silverstein Properties, and Cantor Fitzgerald for Swell Apartments, a 200-unit luxury multifamily community completed in 2024 in Seattle's Yesler Terrace neighborhood. The property features a mix of market-rate and affordable residences near major employers including Amazon, Microsoft, Costco, and Starbucks, with direct access to the Seattle Streetcar and I-5.
stories.impact: Indicates lender appetite for newly built luxury multifamily with mixed-income components in Seattle near major tech employer clusters. Refinancing at year-1 post-delivery signals strong property performance and valuation. For developers: validates Seattle's Yesler Terrace and similar infill neighborhoods with transit and tech-job proximity as fundamentally sound; expect continued capital availability for similar product in Seattle and comparable West Coast tech metros.

stories.title: Insignia Revamping Discounted Atlanta-Area Office Property
stories.excerpt: Insignia plans to spend over $10 million to revamp a large office complex in Vinings that was formerly Home Depot’s headquarters. The property at 2727 Paces Ferry has approximately 640,000 square feet of office space. It has two 18-story towers. The Atlanta Business Chronicle reports that Insignia paid just $21.75 million for the property, having purchased it from a group that had fallen behind on its mortgage payments. The price for the massive office complex comes out to $34 a square foot. The renovation will add a coffee bar and café, tenant lounge and library, conference facilities, coworking areas, restaurant space and indoor-outdoor gathering areas. Newmark’s Craig Kalinowski and Brad Kirchner are the exclusive office leasing agents for the project. Insignia has several other redevelopments underway across metro Atlanta. Dunwoody City Council recently approved a plan to redevelop a local office property into more than 100 townhomes on property owned by an Insignia affiliate. The post Insignia Revamping Discounted Atlanta-Area Office Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Insignia purchased former Home Depot HQ (640k SF office, 2 towers) in Vinings for $21.75M ($34/SF).
Planning $10M+ renovation adding café, coworking, restaurant, and gathering spaces.
Redevelopment reflects broader Atlanta office-to-mixed-use conversion and office distress thesis.
stories.summary: Insignia purchased the 640,000-square-foot former Home Depot headquarters at 2727 Paces Ferry in Vinings, Atlanta, for $21.75 million ($34 per square foot) from a distressed seller. The company plans to invest over $10 million in renovations including café, coworking, restaurant, and gathering amenities. Newmark is the exclusive leasing agent.
stories.impact: Confirms sustained office market distress in Atlanta and increasing developer willingness to repurpose large Class A office towers. The steep discount ($34/SF) and Insignia's concurrent townhome redevelopment plan (100+ units in Dunwoody approved by council) suggest conversion-to-residential may follow amenitization. Monitor for office-to-multifamily conversion pipeline in Atlanta's metro; depressed office values and vacancy could create development opportunities for forward-thinking operators acquiring at distressed pricing.

stories.title: Market Shifts, New York’s Uniqueness Mean Mamdani’s Grocery Plan Could Work
stories.excerpt: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to get the city into the subsidized grocery business. As his administration seeks a seasoned partner this fall to run its planned quintet of government-supported grocery stores, strong opposition means it won’t sail through the express checkout lane. Plus, a pair of new lawsuits could stop the scheme faster than you can cancel an Instacart order, and many critics decry the initiative as the first step in a descent into socialism. Yet, commercial real estate and grocery pros say the idea could work, though key business and financial details remain to be settled. The suits were filed weeks after the administration opened up bidding for a private-sector operator to run five planned stores, one in each borough, and seasoned grocery industry veterans may be in the mix to be part of one of the most high-profile measures in the mayor’s agenda to possibly make life in New York less expensive. Mamdani announced the initiative early in his term, later specifying that city stores would discount prices by 30 percent on essentials such as produce, meat and seafood, and by 20 percent on items including milk and bread. The stores won’t sell alcohol, tobacco or nicotine, but will stock halal, kosher, diabetic-friendly and gluten-free products. Mamdani says this will cut the average New Yorker’s grocery bill by about $90 a month — roughly $1,000 a year. “In the wealthiest city, in the wealthiest country in the history of the world, no New Yorker should have to worry about being able to afford to feed their family,” Mamdani said in a July 27 press conference announcing the request for proposals by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC). Prospective operators of the five planned stores can submit plans until Oct. 16, the agency said. bullets: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans five subsidized city-owned grocery stores, one per borough.
Stores to offer 30% discounts on produce, meat, bread, milk; seeking private-sector operator partner.
Initiative faces lawsuits and political opposition; commercial real estate and grocery pros see potential.
stories.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a plan to open five government-subsidized grocery stores across the city's five boroughs offering 30 percent discounts on staple items. The administration is seeking a private-sector operator to run the stores this fall. The initiative faces legal challenges and political opposition, though retail and real estate professionals believe the model could succeed if key business and financial details are resolved.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily development; primarily a retail/urban policy story. However, if implemented, subsidized groceries signal city commitment to affordability and may modestly strengthen residential desirability in underserved neighborhoods, particularly outer boroughs. Monitor site selection and neighborhood impacts; new grocery anchors could support mixed-use development in food deserts near emerging residential clusters, but execution risk is high given legal challenges.

stories.title: RISE Obtains $101M Bridge Loan for Jax Apartments
stories.excerpt: BWE secured a $101 million bridge loan with HPS, a part of BlackRock, to refinance RISE at Glen Kernan Park, a newly delivered 308-unit luxury active adult (55+) community in Jacksonville, Florida. BWE’s Andy Effler headed up a team made up of Sam Miller, Conor Lee, Paul Smith, Chad Kiner and AJ Mangan. The non-recourse, floating-rate loan, which has a three-year initial term with two additional one-year extension options, allows RISE to retire the senior construction loan (BSP) and the mezzanine loan (Pearlmark Real Estate), and to fund an interest and carry reserve while the property is leasing up. RISE at Glen Kernan Park consists of 109 one-bedroom and 127 two-bedroom apartments, as well as 72 single-story cottage units with attached garages. As an institutional quality, lifestyle-driven product, the community has a wide range of amenities for residents, including a clubhouse, fitness facility, pool, pickleball courts, and a bar and lounge. The units feature screened-in balconies and patios. The post RISE Obtains $101M Bridge Loan for Jax Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BWE obtained $101M bridge loan from HPS (BlackRock) to refinance RISE at Glen Kernan Park, Jacksonville.
308-unit luxury 55+ active adult community with mix of apartments and cottages; newly delivered.
Floating-rate, three-year initial term with two one-year extension options; non-recourse structure.
stories.summary: BWE secured a $101 million floating-rate bridge loan from HPS (part of BlackRock) to refinance RISE at Glen Kernan Park, a newly delivered 308-unit luxury active adult (55+) community in Jacksonville, Florida. The non-recourse loan has a three-year initial term and two optional one-year extensions. The property includes 109 one-bedroom units, 127 two-bedroom units, and 72 single-story cottages with attached garages, plus amenities including clubhouse, fitness center, pool, pickleball, and bar.
stories.impact: Strong signal of institutional debt appetite for senior housing product in Sunbelt markets. Jacksonville's 55+ demographic tailwinds and successful lease-up support refinancing at scale. Validates lifestyle-driven active adult as institutional-quality asset class. For developers: confirms Jacksonville as strong senior housing market with investor backing; expect sustained capital availability for well-positioned 55+ communities in Florida and broader Southeast through construction and stabilization phases.

stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Hyatt Regency in Jersey City Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $100 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by a 351-key waterfront Hyatt Regency hotel in Jersey City, N.J., has been sent to special servicing due to an imminent maturity default, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit Analytics. The $100 million loan — which makes up portions of the CGCMT 2016-P5, CGCMT 2016-P6, and CMBX.10 conduit deals — is expected to default after the sponsorship team stated it would be unable to pay off the loan ahead of its October 2026 maturity. Taconic Capital Advisors and HEI Hotels & Resorts purchased the Hyatt Regency from Veris Residential and Hyatt Hotels in December 2022 for $117 million. Since the 2016 origination of the three CMBS loans, the Hyatt Regency has had only one year — 2016 — when its net cash flow met the levels underwritten on the debt. In fact, the hotel reported negative cash flow in 2024, and its net income came out to 68 percent less than its underwritten expectations in 2025. Morningstar Credit noted that it expects “a loan extension or forbearance as a resolution strategy.” Located at 2 Exchange Place in Downtown Jersey City, the Hyatt Regency sits on a pier directly on the Hudson River Waterfront Walkway. It features more than 20,000 square feet of event space as well as a fitness center, self-parking garage and an on-site restaurant. The hotel is a five-minute walk from a New Jersey PATH train with access into Manhattan. The Hyatt Regency opened in 2002. Taconic Capital Advisors did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hyatt Regency Jersey City ($100M CMBS loan) sent to special servicing; imminent maturity default.
351-key waterfront hotel; Taconic/HEI purchased for $117M in Dec 2022; negative 2024 cash flow.
Only one year (2016) of underwritten cash flow performance; 2025 net income 68% below projection.
stories.summary: A $100 million CMBS loan secured by the 351-key Hyatt Regency waterfront hotel in Jersey City has been sent to special servicing due to an anticipated maturity default in October 2026. Taconic Capital Advisors and HEI Hotels & Resorts purchased the property in December 2022 for $117 million. The hotel has only met underwritten cash flow expectations once since loan origination in 2016 and reported negative cash flow in 2024 and net income 68 percent below expectations in 2025. Morningstar expects extension or forbearance as the likely resolution.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Highlights broader hospitality distress and CMBS maturity wall risks, particularly for waterfront urban assets. Underscores hotel underwriting failures and asset quality concerns in securitized debt pools; reinforces elevated capital costs and stricter underwriting for all asset classes, including multifamily. Developers in NYC/NJ market should monitor for any contagion effects on mixed-use/hospitality conversion discussions.

stories.title: Stockdale Capital Partners Aims for $300M in Loans by 2028 Via New Credit Platform
stories.excerpt: Stockdale Capital Partners, a vertically integrated, Los Angeles-based real estate investment firm, has launched a real estate credit platform that aims to make $300 million worth of loans in the next 12 months. The new credit platform will specialize in deploying capital as senior bridge loans, mezzanine debt, special situation investments and even note purchases across numerous asset classes and different U.S. regions. Loans will vary in size but are likely to range between $15 million and $75 million, and prioritize office, life sciences and hospitality assets, according to a release. Commercial Mortgage Alert first reported the news. Stockdale Capital Partners has tapped Alec Maki, who has spent the last seven years at Fortress Investment Group specializing in real estate debt origination, for the role of senior vice president of credit investments. Maki will work alongside an old Fortress ally, Chase Jensen, now Stockdale’s managing director of acquisitions. “By leveraging the firm’s vertically integrated operational expertise across asset classes, we will be able underwrite transactions more efficiently, better assess risks with greater conviction, and structure flexible capital solutions for borrowers facing complex situations,” said Maki in a statement. Daniel Michaels, Stockdale’s co-founder and managing partner, said the firm aims to leverage its ever-expanding operating platform — the firm manages $4.5 billion of assets — to originate debt investments “with greater scale, focus and consistency.” “We see tremendous opportunity to build a premier real estate credit platform,” said Michaels. Brian Pascus can be reached by bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Stockdale Capital Partners launched real estate credit platform; targets $300M loans in 12 months.
Loan range $15M–$75M; focus on senior bridge, mezzanine, special situations; office, life sciences, hospitality.
Hired Alec Maki (ex-Fortress) as SVP; paired with Chase Jensen (ex-Fortress) for underwriting synergy.
stories.summary: Stockdale Capital Partners, a vertically integrated Los Angeles-based real estate investment firm, launched a new real estate credit platform targeting $300 million in loan originations within 12 months. The platform will deploy capital as senior bridge loans, mezzanine debt, special situation investments, and note purchases. Loan sizes will range from $15 million to $75 million, with priority focus on office, life sciences, and hospitality assets across the U.S. Alec Maki (formerly Fortress) was hired as senior vice president of credit investments.
stories.impact: Modest positive signal for multifamily debt availability. While Stockdale's stated focus is office, life sciences, and hospitality, the platform's $300M scale and senior bridge/mezzanine appetite could create competitive pressure on pricing and terms for development loans in secondary/tertiary markets. The use of Fortress talent signals disciplined underwriting; monitor Stockdale's actual deployment in Q4–2025 to see if multifamily gets allocation or remains sidelined.

stories.title: Property Operations Platform Visitt Teams With VendorPM
stories.excerpt: Visitt, an artificial intelligence-native property operations platform, and VendorPM, a leading vendor life cycle management company, announced Tuesday a partnership to create what they describe as a more unified approach to managing buildings and vendors. By bringing together VendorPM’s life cycle management capabilities with the day-to-day operational workflows in Visitt, the partnership aims to provide property teams with a streamlined way to manage building operations, while ensuring vendors meet organization- and building-specific compliance requirements. “What’s special about this is that, basically for more than two decades, vendors who interact on the daily basis with properties were basically disconnected from the daily operations,” said Jonathan Kroll, co-founder and chief product officer at Manhattan-based Visitt. “The reason is that most of the vendor work was managed outside of the system, creating visibility and compliance gaps, because these vendors should be compliant with the property requirements. “So, because everything was managed outside and sometimes even over emails, the vendor work wasn’t tracked at all. Basically, what we are doing with this partnership is taking the innovation that VendorPM brought into the vendor space and integrating it with daily operations.” The consolidation happening in commercial real estate has companies looking to integrate more technologies into one platform, Kroll explained. Property management companies are relying more on vendors, while owner-operators are looking to lower costs by not doing everything in-house. The result is a greater reliance on vendors, which Visitt and VendorPM envision as valuing their partnership higher and growing in the long run. “Technology consolidation is becoming increasingly important for property teams that are looking to work more efficiently without adding complexity to their day-to-day operations,” Itay Oren, CEO of Visitt, said in a statemen
bullets: Visitt (AI property ops platform) partnered with VendorPM (vendor lifecycle management) for unified operations.
Integration aims to connect daily vendor workflows with compliance and property operations systems.
Addresses decades-old disconnect between vendor management and building operations visibility.
stories.summary: Visitt, an AI-native property operations platform, partnered with VendorPM, a vendor lifecycle management company, to integrate vendor workflows with day-to-day property operations. The partnership aims to create unified visibility and compliance management for building vendors and operations teams, addressing a historically disconnected workflow that created gaps in compliance and operational transparency.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development and capital deployment. This is a property operations/technology story relevant to asset management and NOI optimization post-delivery. Developers and owners should monitor adoption of such tools for operational efficiency gains, but the announcement does not signal shifts in demand, supply, financing, or construction costs.
